rules.statement: An appellate court should not disturb the findings of fact without strong evidence to the contrary, especially when the trial judge had the opportunity to observe witnesses.
rules.supporting_quote: "If the evidence as a whole can reasonably be regarded as justifying the conclusion arrived at at the trial, and especially if that conclusion has been arrived at on conflicting testimony by a tribunal which saw and heard the witnesses, the appellate court will bearing mind that it has not enjoyed this opportunity and that the view of the trial judge as to where credibility lies is entitled to great weight."
